dataset.description:
Data Management Plan of the FishEdge project: "Fish biodiversity on the edge of a warming Mediterranean Sea"

Coastal Mediterranean ecosystems are increasingly impacted by climate warming, which threatens their unique indigenous fishes. In addition, over 100 non-indigenous species from the Red Sea have been colonizing the Mediterranean Sea, including herbivorous rabbitfishes that overgraze on algae. It is therefore critical to better understand how warming affects biodiversity, biology and roles of indigenous and non-indigenous fishes.
The Fish-edge project will address these issues using scientific diving in 5 Crete coastal ecosystems which are at the edge of both warming and invasion.
Fish will be comprehensively censused using eDNA and their abundance estimated from video transects. 
Remote cameras will be used to assess herbivory rate. 
Stress and growth rate will be measured on sampled individuals of 1 indigenous and 3 non-indigenous species.

format:
We will be collecting images (jpg or png, probably) of seascape of study sites and of sampled fishes.
We will be collecting underwater videos (mp4).
We will be collecting DNA sequences (FASTQ) and creating bioinformatics outputs (FASTA, TSV, TXT).
We will be collecting measurements from lab analysis of fish tissues in spreadsheets (CSV or excel).
We will be generating data related to fish biodiversity in spreadsheets (CSV or excel).
